scenarios.title: Bounded Rust integer kernel panic and arithmetic checks
goals: Check overflow, panics, and approved integer postconditions in a small kernel
constraints: Explicit input domain and unwind completeness
questions: Which overflow semantics are intended?
Are called dependencies and Rust features supported by the pinned Kani release?

alternatives.reason: Deductive contracts for unbounded mathematical intent; requires supported-source adaptation

scenarios.assurance: Checks enabled safety properties and assertions for all inputs represented by a harness, subject to complete unwinding, models, assumptions, and tool soundness.
does_not_establish: Unbounded input sizes beyond harness bounds
scenarios.tool_version: Unknown compatibility; pin Kani and its matching Rust toolchain after feature inspection.

examples.scope: Official bounded harness tutorial; not reproduction evidence

work_items.property: Resolve integer semantics, call graph, input domain, and release support
acceptance: Record source-backed intent and unsupported features
Obtain explicit approval for inferred contracts

work_items.property: Check approved integer postconditions and absence of enabled panic/overflow failures in the declared harness domain
acceptance: Pin toolchain and retain exact harness and commands
Retain full output and successful unwinding assertions; report bounds and failures

scenarios.title: Bounded Rust slice and buffer indexing
goals: Find out-of-bounds access and check small-buffer functional assertions
questions: What buffer sizes and preconditions are legitimate?
Are loops completely unwound for that domain?

alternatives.reason: Sequence specifications can cover arbitrary lengths after proof adaptation

scenarios.assurance: Enabled checks and assertions over the stated finite harness domain with complete unwinding.
does_not_establish: Coverage of excluded dependencies or models
scenarios.tool_version: Unknown compatibility; pin Kani/Rust and inspect allocation and library support.

examples.scope: Official slice initialization tutorial; not executed here

work_items.property: Resolve valid lengths, indexing intent, dependencies, and bounds
acceptance: Document length domain and all assumptions
Inspect existing tests for off-by-one requirements

work_items.property: Check approved slice safety and postconditions for explicitly bounded lengths
acceptance: Preserve counterexamples and exact bounds
Require successful unwinding assertions and full check output

scenarios.title: Isolated sequential Rust unsafe-memory harness
goals: Check supported undefined-behavior classes in an isolated unsafe operation
constraints: Explicit allocation, pointer validity, and aliasing assumptions
Inspect tool UB coverage rather than claiming all UB is checked
questions: Which UB checks are supported?
Does the harness model real caller obligations without assuming away bugs?

alternatives.reason: Dynamic UB detection for executed paths, not exhaustive proof

scenarios.assurance: Supported enabled UB checks over the modeled harness domain; coverage depends on the pinned Kani release.
does_not_establish: Absence of every Rust UB class
Soundness of arbitrary unsafe abstractions or FFI
scenarios.tool_version: Unknown compatibility; inspect the pinned release's UB and feature support.

work_items.property: Map unsafe caller obligations and supported UB checks
acceptance: Inventory allocations, lifetimes, aliases, and boundary assumptions
List unsupported UB checks explicitly

work_items.property: Check supported memory-safety obligations for the approved bounded unsafe harness
acceptance: Retain harness, assumptions, exact command, tool versions, and complete output
Do not label partial UB coverage complete memory-safety proof

scenarios.title: Deductive contracts for an adaptable Rust integer kernel
goals: Prove approved pre/postconditions without enumerating bounded executions
constraints: Willingness to adapt supported Rust into Verus
questions: Can the kernel and callees be represented in the supported subset?
Who approves the mathematical contract and migration?

alternatives.reason: Bounded harness checks may require less production-source adaptation

scenarios.assurance: Deductive verification of stated contracts for translated/adapted Verus code, subject to trusted specifications, external bodies, and the verifier/compiler trust boundary.
does_not_establish: Correctness of unstated requirements or the compiler
scenarios.tool_version: Unknown compatibility; pin a Verus release and required Rust toolchain; inspect every callee.

work_items.property: Establish a source-to-contract mapping and Verus subset feasibility
acceptance: Record trusted boundaries and migration scope
Obtain approval for contracts and production adaptation

work_items.property: Deductively verify the approved integer pre/postconditions in adapted Verus source
acceptance: Retain exact verifier output, version, source, and assumptions
Inventory external_body, admits, and trusted declarations; do not hide proof gaps

scenarios.title: Sequence specifications for an adaptable Rust buffer algorithm
goals: Prove length, indexing, and approved sequence postconditions using invariants
questions: What sequence relation defines success?
Are container APIs supported or explicitly trusted?

alternatives.reason: Finite buffers can be checked with smaller initial proof effort

scenarios.assurance: Proof of stated sequence invariants and postconditions in adapted Verus code under declared preconditions and trusted APIs.
does_not_establish: An automatic proof of the original unadapted application
scenarios.tool_version: Unknown compatibility; inspect release-specific container and borrowing support.

work_items.property: Resolve sequence semantics and supported container boundaries
acceptance: Map source operations to specification relations
List adaptation and trusted API obligations

work_items.property: Prove the approved sequence relation with explicit loop invariants
acceptance: Retain proof source, exact tool output, and trusted-boundary inventory
Review correspondence to original behavior before integration

scenarios.title: Verified-source algorithm replacement and code generation
goals: Specify and verify a small replacement kernel written in Dafny
constraints: Explicit opt-in to verified-source replacement/code generation
Review generated-language integration and compiler trust
questions: Is rewriting this kernel in Dafny acceptable?
Which supported compilation target and integration boundary are required?

alternatives.reason: Avoid rewriting where a supported native-language scenario exists

scenarios.assurance: Dafny verifies stated contracts of Dafny source; approved compilation can produce target-language code with separate integration and compiler trust obligations.
does_not_establish: Verification of arbitrary existing Rust/C/C++/other source
Equivalence of replacement to existing code without a separate argument
scenarios.tool_version: Unknown compatibility; pin Dafny and a supported backend, runtime, and integration toolchain.

work_items.property: Establish rewrite approval, contract, target backend, and equivalence obligations
acceptance: Explicitly approve verified-source adoption rather than native-source verification
Document API, runtime, build, and trust boundaries

work_items.property: Verify the approved replacement in Dafny and review generated-code integration
acceptance: Retain Dafny source, proof output, compiler/backend versions, and commands
Provide separate correspondence and integration evidence; never label original code verified
